verdict: UiPath grew revenue 13% to $410M and ARR 12% to $1.94B, and leaner costs turned last year's operating loss into a $32M GAAP operating profit and $36M of net income.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $410M, vs $362M a year ago

kpis.label: ARR
kpis.note: Annualized renewal run-rate, up 12% YoY; net retention 109%

kpis.label: Operating income (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs a $20M loss a year ago; non-GAAP operating income was $89M

segments.name: Subscription services
segments.note: Recurring subscriptions to the automation platform, plus support — the core, predictable revenue. Up 12%.

segments.name: Licenses
segments.note: Software licenses sold for a term. Up 10%.

segments.name: Professional services & other
segments.note: Helping customers set up and run automations. Up 82% — fast-growing, but it costs more to deliver than it brings in.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big companies — the biggest running cost, though it fell slightly YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, including its AI agent tools. Down 15% YoY as last year's spending was trimmed.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Down 5% YoY.

otherDetail: Interest income of $10.8M on cash and investments, plus $10.5M of other income, net.
follow100Note: The rows above Kept as profit add to $100; Kept as profit is what was left of each $100 after all costs, other income and tax.

takeaways.title: Growth held steady
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 13% to $410M, and ARR — the annualized value of subscription contracts — rose 12% to $1.938B, with $37M of net new ARR. Existing customers expanded their spending at a 109% net retention rate.

takeaways.title: High margins, one soft spot
takeaways.text: Gross margin was 80%. Licenses and subscriptions are very profitable to deliver; professional services is not — it brought in $20M and cost $39M to deliver, a loss-making line that grew 82%.

takeaways.title: Back to GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Operating income was $32M, vs a $20M loss a year ago, because revenue grew while total operating expenses fell 6% to $298M. Net income was $36M. On the company's non-GAAP basis (leaving out $45M of stock pay and other items), operating income was $89M.

oneTimers: Operating expenses include $45.0M of stock-based compensation and $5.0M of restructuring costs in the quarter — the main reasons GAAP operating income ($32M) is well below the company's non-GAAP figure ($89M).
General and administrative costs include a $0.8M increase in the fair value of contingent consideration owed on past acquisitions.
